I have been using smart locks for five or six years, and during that time I have tried quite a few models. For most people, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a wide variety of unlocking methods. Whether you prefer fingerprints or a keypad, it has you covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a column series dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to the Apple smart home framework.

Supports Apple Home, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ says the Bolt Fingerprint is its first smart lock with full Apple Home integration, and honestly, that's exactly what drew me in. To this day I still miss Touch ID on my iPhone. You can lock or unlock it through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV as a home hub, you can slot it into automations and scenes like any other Apple Home accessory — and control it from anywhere.

However, I noticed one thing that for me is missing: Home Key support. If I could just tap my iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door, this lock would be perfect. That's its shortcoming, but it's not a deal-breaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ adds this feature in the next generation, because once Home Key is supported, this lock would go from good to nearly perfect. It is also compatible with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT, so no matter which smart home platform you prefer — or even if you want to switch later — it's covered. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, so basic remote control through its app doesn't require an extra bridge.

More unlocking methods than you can shake a stick at

The unlocking options on the Bolt Fingerprint are genuinely impressive. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints and 50 codes. You can unlock through the mobile app, have it unlock automatically as you approach the door, or use voice control via Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys come in the box, so even if the battery dies, you won't find yourself locked out. For me, a smart lock that doesn't include a physical key as backup isn't even worth considering.

You can set up to 50 custom codes, and you can also generate one-time or time-limited codes for friends, visitors, or your cleaning lady. If you're renting out your place, this feature alone is well worth the price.

It also has a Lockout mode that temporarily disables all electronic access, including codes and app access. For anyone about to head off on a trip and wants extra peace of mind while the house is empty, this is really useful. I never would have thought a smart lock would have something like this, but it is a nice bonus.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

Over the past few years I have installed more smart locks than I can count, so for me the process is already old hat. As long as you have the right tools on hand, it's done in about ten minutes. If you're replacing an existing deadbolt, no wiring or drilling is required. You just need a Phillips screwdriver, though it's worth swapping out the strike plate on the door frame while you're at it.

Once you scan the lock into your Apple Home setup and assign it to a room, you can control it through the Home app, or add it to automations and scenes to trigger multiple actions at once — like the lights coming on when the door unlocks.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint wrap-up

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a really solid choice. In day-to-day use, fingerprint unlocking quickly becomes your go-to method. Installation is straightforward too. I've had it on my office door for a while now, because I often have laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out and I wanted an extra layer of security. I love how it automatically unlocks as I approach, and I can also see who's come and gone. The fingerprint recognition takes me back to the days of Touch ID.

You can pick up the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ website.
